$comment: Pocket Casts Wear OS sticker sheet, rendered from :wear. This is a separate system from the phone catalog rather than the same one at a smaller size. The phone app resolves one of nine user-selectable Theme.ThemeType palettes into ~100 semantic roles behind LocalColors; WearAppTheme instead builds a single Wear Compose `Colors` from the fixed WearColors constants over a black background, with no user choice and no LocalColors at all — so there is exactly one mode here, and it is dark. The components are Wear's too (Chip, ScalingLazyColumn, curved TimeText), with no mobile counterpart. Because the surface is black, the spec declares `display.surface: "dark"`; drop that and the preview server stages these on its default white background, where the light-on-black content disappears. One clean-up was needed before this spec could exist: seven of the module's previews were all named `Preview()` and an eighth in ErrorScreen.kt was a copy-paste of `NotificationScreenPreview`, so they collided both in the render filenames and in any spec that tried to name them. They are renamed after the surface each one actually renders. Everything here is deterministic — fixed strings and fixed state, no ViewModel and no network image loading.
